surfaces.rationale: Pure policy categories, structural identities, admitted observations, and invariant-preserving collections used by the checker. Every declaration is checked under its exact transitive axiom set. The library proves finite-observation classification, declaration/execution decisions and concrete acceptance. The operational adapters collect complete request-indexed jobs through these definitions. Their proofs do not authenticate compiler or filesystem observations, compiled machine code, or semantic adequacy.

Cold-start verification driver with exact proof-bearing argument selection. Recipes are interpreted through a trusted process IO boundary under verify.sh's single external deadline; the proof does not authenticate subprocess execution.

Toolchain-only local provisioning of one shared, read-only Mathlib per pinned revision and toolchain. The proofs concern the pure decisions it executes: receipt admission is sound, only a link to the shared checkout is kept for Mathlib, removal from a copy is confined to links and clean Git checkouts, only a receipt that names a shared directory identifies it for removal, registering drops no copy, and a shared directory is removed only when it is not the current one and no registered copy still links it. Git, Lake, cp, chmod, ln, rename, file locking and Mathlib's cache tool are trusted process and filesystem effects that the proofs do not authenticate.

Pure observation-validation contracts used by Lean qualification drivers. Soundness, completeness, first-refusal and composition concern the supplied Lean data, not authenticity of process/filesystem/compiler observations. Runtime and library boundaries are reported separately.

The rule registry and the pure checker projections the operational checker executes: claim request, scope admission for every supplied coordinate check, transcript-coordinate and source-range admission for every UTF-16 column function, declaration rules and reasons, foundation labels, execution rules and failure text, census assembly from decoded manifest and Lake records, and the report account every rendered success and completed status projects from one accepted run. Their contracts concern the supplied declarations, transcripts and records; Lean's UTF-16 column function, manifest parsing, Lake loading, environment extraction, compiler and filesystem observations stay in the excluded adapters.
The Audit library contains Real-based examples. Every declaration is still labeled from its own exact axiom set under standard §4.5.

The complete-application dogfooding surface: admission, update, and strict state/error composition contracts are proved about the definitions auditApp runs, alongside the retained total fold. The limiter state/error operations and their proofs are choice-free; the input parser and dependent required-contract interface transitively use Classical.choice through core String internals, as does the IO root. The surface claim is standard-logical and each declaration retains its exact axiom report. The IO shell is trusted execution substrate, so the execution mode stays report.

excluded-libraries.rationale: Positive controls and intentionally invalid mutations are queryable for exact contamination checks but are not part of the conforming Audit surface.

Operational Lean checker code is not a conforming proof surface; acceptance does not re-elaborate or report its declarations. It holds the adapters around the claimed RegulaPolicy and RegulaCore decisions: Lake and environment observation, frontend transcripts, Lean's LSP UTF-16 column conversion, compiler and worker processes, JSON transport, filesystem provenance and text rendering. Its external observation paths are mutation-qualified separately; its proved transport-admission theorems are kernel-checked by the warning-as-error lake build and bounded to Standard-Logical by an in-module collectAxioms ceiling. Outside acceptance, the self-audit diagnostic (./scripts/verify.sh diagnostics self-audit) kernel-admits every module and decides every declaration with the proved operational decision RegulaPolicy.operationalFailure: the Standard-Logical declaration rules, with authored unsafe/partial declarations and the pinned toolchain's Lake axioms in non-proposition definitions reported rather than failed, and module documentation required.

excluded-executables.rationale: Operational qualification dispatcher and IO adapters in the excluded Regula library. It invokes proved observation oracles from the positive RegulaQualification library; filesystem, process and compiler observations are not authenticated by those proofs.

Every text it prints, its command parser and their proofs are the claimed RegulaCore.Guidance and RegulaCore.Feedback definitions; the root only prints them and sets the exit code.

Its root module belongs to the excluded Regula library; it calls an external judgment service only when explicitly run, is never part of offline acceptance, and its screened results are not conforming evidence. Its pure decisions are proved in the claimed RegulaPolicy.Screening and RegulaCore.Screening modules.
